channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: 1 GW Data Centers to Be Established in Karakalpakstan
item.description: A large-scale project to create a technopark with 1 GW data centers will be implemented in the Nukus district of Karakalpakstan. Renewable energy sources will power the complex, with construction of new substations and transmission lines planned. The first phase is expected by late 2027.

item.title: Solar Panels Provide Drinking Water to Nearly 100 Households
item.description: In the Shurchin district of Surkhandarya region, solar panels have been installed to provide drinking water to nearly 100 households. The 35 kW⋅h solar installation was funded by a 150 million soum grant awarded to the Makhalla "Tamshush" for winning a competition.

item.title: Leather and Footwear Industrial Zone Worth $28 Million Established in Andijan
item.description: A leather and footwear industrial zone valued at $28 million has been established in Andijan. The complex will implement 17 projects, creating approximately 2,500 new jobs. This initiative aims to boost the region's manufacturing sector.

item.title: Conference on Modern Approaches to Engineering Education Held in Tashkent
item.description: Tashkent Institute of Textile and Light Industry hosted an international conference on modern engineering education. The event, part of the Erasmus+ project TEX4FUTURE, focused on training qualified personnel for modern mechanical engineering and industry modernization. Participants discussed digital transformation and international academic cooperation.

item.title: Artificial Intelligence and Dual Education Integrated into Andijan's Textile Industry
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited the "Eco Cotton" enterprise in Andijan, which produces knitwear using local raw materials and modern technology. The facility employs 1,000 people, utilizes AI and dual education for staff training, and adheres to environmental standards. It expects to contribute 25 billion soms annually to the state budget.

item.title: Bishkek police seize over 6,000 doses of synthetic drugs
item.description: Two individuals were detained in Bishkek on suspicion of distributing synthetic drugs via hidden caches. Authorities seized over 1 kilogram of Alpha-PVP, valued at over 4 million Kyrgyz soms, which could have been divided into more than 6,000 doses.

item.title: Uzbek President proposes attracting businesses to create jobs for low-income citizens
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev proposed greater involvement of entrepreneurs in creating jobs for low-income citizens, offering preferential loans and tax conditions. He emphasized the need for targeted assistance and empowering local authorities to address poverty and employment issues.

item.title: Uztelecom Expands Satellite Communication in Uzbekistan with Amazon Leo Partnership
item.description: Uztelecom has signed an agreement with Amazon Leo to become an authorized distributor in Uzbekistan. This partnership aims to expand satellite communication capabilities and advance the country's digital infrastructure. The collaboration is expected to bring new opportunities for digital development.

item.title: Tajikistan and China to Expand Cooperation in Civil Servant Training
item.description: Tajikistan's Academy of Public Administration and Lanzhou University of Technology signed a Memorandum of Understanding to enhance cooperation in education, research, and academic exchange. The agreement includes faculty and student exchanges, joint research on Central Asia, and training programs for Tajik civil servants.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Direct Bishkek-Sanya Flights to China
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has proposed launching direct flights between Bishkek and Sanya, China. The proposal was made by the Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers during a meeting with Chinese Premier Li Qiang. Discussions also covered railway construction, road projects, and cooperation in energy and digital economy.

item.title: Kyrgyz Parliament Approves Self-Ban on Real Estate Transactions in First Reading
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's parliament has approved amendments allowing citizens to impose a self-ban on real estate transactions for up to 72 hours. Proposed by MP Dastan Bekeshev, the measure aims to combat rising real estate fraud, particularly for elderly citizens, by providing a mechanism similar to self-banning loans.

item.title: Second International Textile Forum Opens in Dushanbe, Tajikistan
item.description: The Second International Textile Forum, 'Tajikistan-2026,' opened in Dushanbe on September 23, 2026. Organized by the Ministry of Industry and New Technologies, the forum brings together government and business representatives from 15 countries to discuss industry development, investment, and international experience.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes Direct Bishkek-Sanya Flight Route to China
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has suggested China consider opening a direct flight route between Bishkek and the resort city of Sanya. The proposal was made by Cabinet Chairman Adylbek Kasymaliev during a meeting with Chinese Premier Li Qiang in Hangzhou.

item.title: Second Phase of Andijan International Airport Reconstruction Progressing Rapidly
item.description: The second phase of reconstruction at Andijan International Airport is advancing quickly, modernizing the facility and expanding its capabilities. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev inspected the ongoing work, which began after his previous directives in 2021 and 2023.

item.title: New School Buildings Commissioned in Kurush and Tagoyak Villages, Spitamen District
item.description: Two new school buildings were opened in the Spitamen district of Tajikistan's Sughd region on September 22, 2026, coinciding with the 35th anniversary of Tajikistan's independence. The Ministry of Education and Science reported the event, attended by education officials and local authorities.

item.title: President Mirziyoyev Visits Andijan-Huanya International Technical School
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev visited the Andijan-Huanya International Technical School to familiarize himself with the conditions created for training qualified personnel for industrial enterprises. He also spoke with students and investors.

item.title: Kazakhstan's President Tokayev Urges Against Politicizing the Russian Language
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev called for not turning the Russian language into a political issue. He emphasized that language should serve to unite people and foster mutual understanding within the country.

item.title: Tajikistan Trains State Officials on Cybersecurity Incident Response
item.description: From September 21-23, 2026, Tajikistan's Agency for Innovation and Digital Technologies hosted a national cybersecurity training course. The goal was to enhance state bodies' readiness to detect, analyze, and respond to cyber incidents.

item.title: World Bank Economist Advises Uzbekistan Against Resisting WTO Integration
item.description: Ayhan Kose, Deputy Chief Economist at the World Bank, advised Uzbekistan not to resist integration into the World Trade Organization (WTO). He stated that joining the WTO would increase the country's resilience to global shocks. Kose discussed this during a Research Talks project with the Central Bank of Uzbekistan.

item.title: Tourism Operators from Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Belarus to Expand Cooperation
item.description: Tourism representatives from Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Belarus met in Dushanbe to discuss expanding direct business contacts and creating joint tourism products. The meeting included officials from tourism committees and operators from the three countries. They explored integrating routes and developing packages for cultural, ecological, and medical tourism.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Expand Freight Wagon Fleet Due to High Demand and Aging Stock
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to expand its freight wagon fleet to meet high demand from domestic producers and trading companies, according to the transport minister. He noted the need for more wagons, citing increased demand and the aging of the current fleet. The new China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway is expected to further boost demand.

item.title: Andijan Region Launches 206 Projects Worth $9.4 Billion, Including Energy and Manufacturing
item.description: President Shavkat Mirziyoyev launched 206 new investment projects totaling $9.4 billion in the Andijan region. Of these, 98 projects worth $2.05 billion have been initiated, and construction has begun on 108 projects valued at $7.35 billion. The projects span various sectors, including energy, manufacturing, and tourism, with international cooperation.

item.title: Central Asia's water balance shifts as glaciers melt and snow cover shrinks
item.description: Climate change accelerates glacier melt and reduces snow cover in Central Asia, creating glacial lakes that pose risks to mountain communities. A scientist explained these changes and their consequences, noting that reduced snow and melting glaciers may decrease water availability in the summer.

item.title: Badakhshan electrification project reconstructs Khorog substation 'Bizmich'
item.description: The 'Bizmich' 35/10 kV substation in Khorog is undergoing reconstruction as part of the 'Electrification of Badakhshan' project, funded by the Tajik government and the European Union. The reconstruction aims to ensure stable and reliable electricity supply for Khorog, especially for the upcoming autumn-winter season.

item.title: Uzbekistan to implement four airport projects under public-private partnerships
item.description: Uzbekistan is pursuing four airport development projects through public-private partnerships, including a new international airport in Tashkent and upgrades in Urgench, Bukhara, Andijan, and Namangan. The transport minister confirmed that initial work has begun on the Tashkent project, with agreements signed with private partners.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Central Election Commission Approves Campaign Financing Rules
item.description: The Central Election Commission of Kyrgyzstan has approved regulations for the formation and use of election funds by presidential candidates. The rules define procedures for candidates and parties, including opening special bank accounts and paying election deposits. The commission will monitor fund usage, and candidates must submit financial reports.

item.title: Parliament Dismisses Supreme Court Judge A. Mukhamedzhanov Due to Death
item.description: The Parliament of Kyrgyzstan has dismissed Supreme Court judge A. Mukhamedzhanov from his post following his death. The decision was made during a parliamentary session. A parliamentary committee had previously recommended his early dismissal. Mukhamedzhanov passed away on July 17 at the age of 67 after a prolonged illness.

item.title: Detention Extended for Former Bishkek Security Chief Eldar Zhakypbekov
item.description: The Pervomaisky District Court in Bishkek has extended the detention of Eldar Zhakypbekov, former head of the National Security Committee's department in the capital, until October 15, 2026. Zhakypbekov, nicknamed 'Edu', was arrested on February 15 and is accused of corruption. Three other individuals also had their detention extended.

item.title: Uzbek Citizen Sentenced to Over 3 Years for Fighting in Ukraine
item.description: A 26-year-old Uzbek citizen, identified as A.Kh., has been sentenced to three years and one month in prison for fighting on the Russian side in the Ukraine conflict. He reportedly signed a military contract to secure his release from a 12-year sentence for drug trafficking in Russia. He was injured in Ukraine.

item.title: Tajikistan and Grenada Sign Visa-Free Travel Agreement
item.description: Tajikistan's Foreign Minister Sirojiddin Mukhriddin and Grenada's Finance Minister Denis Cornwall met in New York and signed an agreement on mutual visa exemption. The agreement, signed on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly session, allows citizens of both countries to travel visa-free.

item.title: Lithuania Halts Job Applications for Citizens of Central Asian Countries
item.description: Lithuania has stopped accepting job applications from citizens of Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, and Kazakhstan. The annual quota for workers from third countries was filled in September, leading to the suspension of new applications.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva Meets with DFC Head Ben Cardey
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva met with DFC head Ben Cardey in the US. During the meeting, they discussed major joint projects initiated in the transport and healthcare sectors.

item.title: Tajikistan and South Korea Agree on Financial Intelligence Exchange
item.description: Tajikistan and South Korea signed 15 new cooperation documents, including a memorandum on exchanging financial intelligence. The agreement aims to combat money laundering and terrorism financing, fostering mutual cooperation and international interaction.

item.title: Tajikistan and Islamic Development Bank Discuss Energy Investments and Rogun HPP
item.description: Tajikistan's Ministry of Finance met with the Islamic Development Bank to discuss investment in the energy sector, focusing on the Rogun HPP for energy security and green energy. They also reviewed cooperation in transport infrastructure and education facilities. Both sides affirmed commitment to ongoing dialogue and priority projects for sustainable development.

item.title: Uzbekistan Explains How Resource Tax Works and Why It's Necessary
item.description: An official explains why high global commodity prices do not equate to excess profits for mining operations in Uzbekistan. The article details how the resource tax accounts for project costs and ensures normal profitability for investors, covering risks and capital investment.

item.title: Saida Mirziyoyeva Leads Uzbekistan Delegation at UN General Assembly 81st Session
item.description: Saida Mirziyoyeva is heading Uzbekistan's delegation at the 81st session of the UN General Assembly. Approximately 130 countries are participating in the session, where the Uzbek delegation listened to speeches from various heads of state during the general debates.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Pakistan to Simplify Cargo Transit Through Ports and Corridors
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has initiated public discussion on a draft law to ratify an agreement with Pakistan on transit trade. The accord aims to regulate transit freedom, use of transport corridors and ports, and customs procedures. A special committee will be established to coordinate efforts between the two nations.

item.title: Akmal Jumanazarov Appointed Chairman of Defense Industry Committee
item.description: Akmal Jumanazarov has been appointed as the Chairman of the Defense Industry Committee under the Cabinet of Ministers. Previously, he headed the Technical Regulation Agency since February 2024. Jumanazarov also served as Deputy Minister of Energy and headed a department within the Cabinet of Ministers.

item.title: Bishkek power engineers increase substation capacity ahead of winter
item.description: In Bishkek, the 'Berlik' substation is increasing the capacity of its second transformer from 16 to 25 thousand kilovolt-amperes. The city's electricity network enterprise reported this. Works are being carried out using a cascade method. The modernization of the city's power grids is planned to continue, with capacity increases also foreseen for the 'Kyzyl-Asker' and 'Central-3' substations.

item.title: Kaspersky Lab begins translating products into Kyrgyz language
item.description: Kaspersky Lab has started translating its products and educational platforms into the Kyrgyz language. The company's Managing Director for Central Asia and Mongolia announced this initiative, which includes adapting the CyberABC educational guide. The project, funded this year, aims to improve digital literacy and cybersecurity in Kyrgyzstan without commercial intent.
